| [NOTE-314](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-314.md) | Calculation of signal detection theory measures | A practical tutorial that gives closed-form SDT measures computed from the hit rate H and false-alarm rate F. They are d′ = Φ⁻¹(H) − Φ⁻¹(F); β = exp{[Φ⁻¹(F)² − Φ⁻¹(H)²]/2}; c = −[Φ⁻¹(H) + Φ⁻¹(F)]/2; the nonparametric A′ and Grier's B″ (single-formula versions, eqs. 3 and 9); A_z = Φ(intercept/√(1+slope²)) from the z-ROC, whose slope is σ_noise/σ_signal; and A_d′ = Φ(d′/√2), which equals 2AFC proportion correct under the d′ assumptions. It also gives one-line commands for seven software packages. Its worked rating example (50 signal and 25 noise trials, noise SD larger than signal SD) shows d′ ranging from 0.84 to 1.86 across criteria. The authors conclude that d′ should not be used without rating-task evidence of equal variance. | Read |
| [NOTE-397](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-397.md) | Yilmaz, Harma & Doğruyol 2021, the MAC-Q in Turkey | An independent validation of the MAC-Q. In Turkish undergraduates (n = 445) seven factors fit the Relevance items (CFI .949, RMSEA .053, SRMR .046) but not the Judgement items (CFI .828) or the full form (CFI .752), as in the original. Family and deference track resistance to change; deference tracks, and fairness counters, opposition to equality. Resource-scarcity primes in Turkey (n = 576) and in a preregistered US MTurk study (n = 921) had no effect. Relevance scores correlate about .1–.3 with prosocial intentions. The seven are strongly intercorrelated. | Read |
| [NOTE-398](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-398.md) | Atari et al. 2023, the MFQ-2 | A new Moral Foundations Questionnaire, built across 25 populations in local languages: 116 candidate items cut to 36, six each for Care, Equality, Proportionality, Loyalty, Authority and Purity, in a "describes me" format. Six factors fit across 19 nations (ESEM CFI .979); reliabilities ω .73–.95; Purity alone fails the alignment invariance threshold. Equality and Proportionality are nearly orthogonal in WEIRD samples. Purity rises most with cultural distance from the U.S. The individualizing–binding split appears in only three national networks. The MFQ-2 predicts criterion scales better than the MFQ-1. | Read |
| [NOTE-412](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-412.md) | Curry, Jones Chesters & Van Lissa 2019, the MAC-Q | A 42-item questionnaire for morality-as-cooperation's seven domains, written by the authors from the theory and reduced to three items per subscale. In UK (n = 1,392) and US (n = 469) online samples, seven factors fit the Relevance items well (CFI .98) and the Judgement items poorly (CFI .87). The two sets cannot be pooled into seven domains (CFI .73); the best model keeps fourteen correlated factors. The MFQ's five factors are not recovered. MFQ purity items are rated about as morally relevant as its loyalty and authority items, which the authors concede contradicts the theory. The data cannot be shared. | Read |
| [NOTE-435](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-435.md) | A Network Theory of Mental Disorders | Borsboom states the network theory as five principles: complexity, symptom-component correspondence, direct causal connections between symptoms, disorders as tightly coupled symptom clusters, and hysteresis. | [NOTE-445](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-445.md) | The Diffusion Decision Model: Theory and Data for Two-Choice Decision Tasks | The full diffusion model (drift v with across-trial SD η, boundaries 0 and a, starting point z with range s_z, non-decision time Ter with range s_t) fitted by the χ² quantile method. In three dot-motion experiments with 14–17 participants difficulty maps to drift alone, speed–accuracy instructions to boundaries alone, and a 75:25 proportion mainly to starting point; RT distribution shape is invariant across conditions. | [NOTE-466](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-466.md) | HDDM: Hierarchical Bayesian Estimation of the Drift-Diffusion Model in Python | HDDM fits the full DDM (v, a, z, t with sv, st, sz) by MCMC in PyMC, with group-level priors such as μ_a ~ Gamma(1.5, 0.75), μ_v ~ N(2, 3), z_j ~ invlogit(N(μ_z, σ_z²)), and the Navarro–Fuss likelihood. A patsy-style regressor lets a parameter vary with a trial covariate. In simulations with 12 subjects and 20–150 trials, hierarchical Bayes had the lowest trimmed recovery error for every parameter and the highest power to detect drift differences and covariate effects, by up to 20% for the latter with larger effects and few trials. | Read |
| [NOTE-484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-484.md) | Bayesian hypothesis testing for psychologists: A tutorial on the Savage–Dickey method | For nested models the Bayes factor for a point null is the ratio of posterior to prior density of the tested parameter at the null value, under the larger model (Eq. 12, derived in Appendix A). It needs the nuisance parameters' prior to be continuous at the null. Worked examples give BF10 ≈ 2.2 where p ≈ .006, and BF01 ≈ 4 in favour of a null of no group difference. | Read |
| [NOTE-957](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-957.md) | Feldman & Lynch — self-generated validity | A theoretical paper, with no new data. When the belief, attitude or intention asked about is not already in memory, the question creates it, and the created answer is later retrieved as an input to other answers and to behaviour; when it is in memory, question order and format still decide which earlier answer is used. An earlier response is used for a later one if it is accessible and more diagnostic than other accessible inputs. Expertise, direct experience and trait involvement reduce the effects, because they supply judgements already formed and rehearsed. | Read |
| [NOTE-990](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-990.md) | Lush, Botan, Scott, Seth, Ward & Dienes — Trait phenomenological control and the rubber hand illusion | Hypnotisability predicted rubber hand illusion reports after both synchronous and asynchronous brushing (n = 353, about half a scale point per SWASH point, rs 0.26), a visual control item as well, and synchronous drift weakly (rs 0.11); it also predicted vicarious pain and mirror touch. | [NOTE-992](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-992.md) | Abdulkarim & Ehrsson — No causal link between hand position sense and limb ownership | A motor slid the hidden hand 8 cm toward or away from the rubber hand during brushing, too slowly to be noticed. Pointing followed it by about 5–6 cm, but questionnaire ownership depended only on synchrony and not on where the hand was moved, in two experiments of 18. With the hand still, the classic synchronous drift and its correlation with the illusion reappeared. The authors conclude drift is not a cause of ownership; the null is from small samples within the illusion's known spatial range. | Read |
| [NOTE-997](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-997.md) | Ehrsson et al. — No specific relationship between hypnotic suggestibility and the rubber hand illusion | A reanalysis of Lush et al.'s (2020) open data, n = 353. The synchronous-minus-asynchronous difference in rubber-hand illusion ratings is unrelated to hypnotisability (rho = -0.066, BF01 = 5.7), is significant in every hypnotisability quartile, and is not changed by explicit suggestions about which condition should work; the hypnotisability correlations Lush et al. report appear equally for the asynchronous condition and an "impossible" control item. The authors conclude the illusion is a perceptual one, "driven primarily by multisensory mechanisms". The reply grants every number and disputes that the asynchronous condition controls for expectation. | Read |

| [NOTE-1001](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1001.md) | Roseboom & Lush — Serious problems with interpreting rubber hand illusion experiments | Resampling 351 synchronous-condition reports from Lush et al. 2020 into 10,000 studies of 20, the authors find that samples from above the median of hypnotisability almost always "find" the rubber hand illusion, and samples from below it find agreement with the ownership statement about 4% of the time. | [NOTE-1003](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1003.md) | Lush & Seth — Reply to: No specific relationship between hypnotic suggestibility and the rubber hand illusion | The reply to Ehrsson et al. accepts their reanalyses and denies their reading: expectancies are higher for synchronous than asynchronous brushing, the difference does not vary with hypnotisability (b = -0.16, P = 0.072, B = 0.07), so a null relation between hypnotisability and the synchrony effect is what demand characteristics predict. | [NOTE-1004](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1004.md) | Longo et al. — What is embodiment? A psychometric approach | 131 people rated 27 statements after synchronous and asynchronous brushing of a rubber hand. Principal components analysis found embodiment of the rubber hand, loss of own hand, movement and affect in both conditions and deafference after asynchrony only; embodiment split into ownership, location and agency. Ownership and location crossed from negative to positive with synchrony and each predicted proprioceptive drift (1.34 cm against 0.30 cm); agency stayed negative. | [NOTE-1005](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1005.md) | Lush — Demand characteristics confound the rubber hand illusion | People told about the rubber hand procedure, but never put through it, expect the illusion statements more than the control statements and more under synchronous than asynchronous brushing (d = 1.40 and 1.05, n = 20), which is the pattern published reports show. So the field's standard controls do not control for suggestion. The paper does not show that the illusion is suggestion, and says so. | Read |
| [NOTE-1009](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1009.md) | Rohde, Di Luca & Ernst — Feeling of ownership and proprioceptive drift do not go hand in hand | With robot stroking and a visual probe of felt finger position, drift toward a rubber hand was as large when the hand was only seen as under synchronous stroking (about 6 cm), and as large under asynchronous stroking interrupted every 10 s; only continuous asynchrony kept it near zero. Ownership by questionnaire needed synchrony. The authors conclude that drift is visuo-proprioceptive integration that asynchrony suppresses, separate from ownership, and not a proxy for it. Groups of ten; the vision-only ownership report is anecdotal. | Read |
| [NOTE-1079](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1079.md) | McFadyen et al. — Doorways do not always cause forgetting | Four conceptual replications from an independent lab. In passive, head-mounted virtual reality, doorways did not lower hits for carried or set-down objects; under a counting load they raised false alarms to recombined probes. Watching or walking a curtained hallway did not change memory for a 16-item grid. The nulls are informative but not direct failures to replicate: movement was passive, and Experiments 3 and 4 used a different memory task. | Read |
